reasoning_traces.think:
The evidence readiness matrix encodes a structured Bayesian framework where each evidence record E is evaluated against activation A, freshness F, trust T, and sample size S. These form a composite readiness state R(E) = f(A, F, T, S). When T ≤ 1 or S < min(S) or F = STALE, then R(E) = BLOCKED. Otherwise, R(E) ∈ {ACTIVE, SHADOW_READY, SHADOW_COLLECTING}. The matrix is a structured table of these states across factors. In GSI, this becomes a probabilistic model where P(factor | evidence) is updated based on R(E). In GSE, R(E) drives state transitions via actionForStatus and factorBlockers. The kernel of this system is the factor blocker logic, which evaluates whether a factor can contribute to inference. If any critical blocker B_c is true, the factor is blocked. Otherwise, it is active. NextBestActions is a derived policy that selects up to five unblocked factors for further processing, ensuring optimal resource allocation under uncertainty. The failure mode occurs when trust normalization drops below 1 or sample size falls below minimum thresholds, leading to systematic blocking of evidence.
